mainTopic: Trees near a boundary: עולא's rule on ביכורים, the sixteen-cubit root zone, and how far overhanging branches must be cut over a neighbor's field or רשות הרבים.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to עולא, who says a tree feeding from land that is not its owner's is exempt from ביכורים. The גמרא answers that the משנה about land of any size is talking about wheat. It then tests עולא against a ברייתא about a tree growing on the border of ארץ ישראל, and explains that ברייתא as a case where a rock splits the roots. אביי explains that roots spread far but only weaken the soil within sixteen cubits. Two reports disagree about what רבי יוחנן said of a tree near the boundary: either its owner is a גזלן, or he brings ביכורים because of the condition יהושע made. A new משנה teaches how much of a neighbor's overhanging tree may be cut, and the גמרא proves that אבא שאול is adding to the first clause. A second משנה covers trees over רשות הרבים. The גמרא discusses judging damage by the present, shows that the רבנן's camel-and-rider measure is higher than רבי יהודה's, and explains that רבי שמעון's concern is אהל הטומאה. The chapter לא יחפור then closes with the הדרן.

steps.title: End of the challenge: tiny land also lets you acquire movables
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the quoted משנה, which together form a challenge to עולא: land of any size obligates ביכורים, and movable property can be acquired along with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and movable property can be acquired together with it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its quote of a משנה that it is using to challenge עולא. The full quote says that land of any size obligates ביכורים, and that movable property can be acquired along with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats even the smallest piece of land as real land that obligates ביכורים. According to עולא, a tree that has very little land around it draws food from the neighbor's soil and should be exempt from ביכורים. So the משנה seems to contradict עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Property that cannot serve as a guarantee for a loan, meaning movable property
Are acquired together with it (the land)
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: This line is only the tail of a longer quote. The part that matters most for the challenge is the earlier phrase, 'land of any size obligates ביכורים', which the גמרא already quoted just before this point.

phrases.english: and are acquired along with it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the small piece of land from the משנה being quoted.

phrases.english: properties that do not serve as a guarantee!
phrases.notes: This means movable things, which a lender cannot collect from a buyer the way he can with land.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְנִקְנִין עִמָּהּ נְכָסִים שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אַחְרָיוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the משנה that began just before this point.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that a tree feeding off land that is not its owner's is exempt from ביכורים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says even a minimal plot obligates ביכורים. A tree on a minimal plot must feed from surrounding land, so by עולא's reasoning it should be exempt.

steps.title: The משנה is talking about wheat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is about wheat, which needs only a tiny amount of soil.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Wheat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא by saying the משנה is not talking about trees at all. It is talking about wheat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wheat grows fully from a small patch of soil and does not reach out into a neighbor's land. So a tiny plot of wheat really is fed by its owner's own land, and it obligates ביכורים. Trees need much more soil, so עולא's rule about trees still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? (a formula that narrows a source to a specific case)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
With wheat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1 by limiting the משנה to wheat.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה was assumed to include trees on a tiny plot.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about wheat, which feeds only from its own small plot, so it does not contradict עולא.

steps.title: The wording 'any size' supports the wheat answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the משנה's own words, 'any size', fit wheat better than trees, and accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact, since it says 'any size'. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its answer by pointing to the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כל שהוא' means truly the smallest bit of land. No normal tree can live on that much soil, but wheat can. So the wording itself shows that the משנה had wheat in mind, and the גמרא accepts the point with 'שמע מינה'.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also exact (the text itself supports this)
Any amount at all, even the smallest
Learn from it (the point is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about land of any size is about wheat, so עולא's rule about trees is not contradicted.

phrases.english: It is also precise, since it teaches:
Of any size.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 2 from the משנה's own wording.
steps.raayaObject: The answer that the משנה is about wheat
steps.raayaSupportSource: The phrase 'כל שהוא' in the משנה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The challenge to עולא is answered.

steps.title: A tree half in ארץ ישראל: רבי's view
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: for a tree growing partly in ארץ ישראל and partly outside it, רבי says each fruit is a mix of טבל and חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a tree that stands partly in ארץ ישראל and partly outside it has טבל and חולין mixed together. This is the opinion of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new source that bears on עולא's idea that a tree draws food from the ground around it. It quotes רבי's opinion in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי holds that the whole tree draws from both lands together. So every fruit carries a mix: part of it is obligated in מעשרות (טבל) and part is exempt (חולין). This idea, that nourishment from different soils blends, is what the גמרא will test against עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source brought as proof)
Produce from which תרומות and מעשרות have not yet been separated
Ordinary produce, here meaning produce exempt from tithes

phrases.english: Come and hear: A tree
part of which is in the Land
and part of which is outside the Land
untithed and non-sacred produce are mixed together,
the words of Rabbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was settled, the גמרא opens a second challenge to עולא with a ברייתא about a tree straddling the border. The challenge itself is stated in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The question of how a tree's nourishment from different soils is viewed, which matters for עולא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a tree straddling the border of ארץ ישראל

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: each part follows its own land
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with רבי: the part growing in ארץ ישראל is obligated and the part growing outside is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: what grows in the obligated place is obligated, and what grows in the exempt place is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the opinion that disagrees with רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל does not see each fruit as a blend. He divides the tree: fruit on the part over ארץ ישראל needs tithing, and fruit on the part outside does not. The two views give the גמרא material to compare with עולא's idea about nourishment from neighboring land.

keyTerms.meaning: What grows in an obligated place (ארץ ישראל)
What grows in an exempt place (outside ארץ ישראל)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי: each fruit of a tree on the border is a mix of טבל and חולין. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: each part follows the land it grows over.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
what grows in an obligated place is obligated,
what grows in an exempt place is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the disagreeing view in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fruit growing over ארץ ישראל must be tithed; fruit growing over land outside ארץ ישראל is exempt.

steps.title: The two opinions are only arguing about בררה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagree only about whether there is בררה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only disagree on this point: one holds there is בררה, and the other holds there is no בררה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the argument in the ברייתא is really about. This is a setup line that prepares the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds יש ברירה: we can say afterward that the fruit on the ארץ ישראל side drew from ארץ ישראל soil. רבי holds אין ברירה: we cannot sort it out, so every fruit is a mix. By saying they argue ONLY about this, the גמרא sets up the inference in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They only disagree up to this point (and no further)
We can determine after the fact which part was which
We cannot determine after the fact which part was which

phrases.english: They only disagree in that
one master holds: there is retroactive designation,
phrases.notes: This first opinion is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who splits the tree into obligated and exempt parts.

phrases.english: and one master holds: there is no retroactive designation;

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (as the first half of the challenge in step 7)
steps.triggerLanguage: עַד כָּאן לָא פְּלִיגִי, אֶלָּא דְּמָר סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the basis of the dispute quoted in steps 4 and 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute between רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל depends only on whether there is בררה.

steps.title: A tree growing entirely outside is exempt by everyone, which challenges עולא
steps.stepSummary: If the only argument is about בררה, then a tree that grew in an exempt place is exempt according to all, which contradicts עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the tree grew in an exempt place, everyone agrees it is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the setup from step 6 to challenge עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to עולא, a tree's roots spread far, so a tree just outside the border could draw food from ארץ ישראל soil. Yet the ברייתא implies that a tree growing entirely outside is exempt according to everyone. This means its roots reaching into ארץ ישראל would not matter, which goes against עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Grew in an exempt place (outside ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: But if it grew in an exempt place,
phrases.notes: He means a tree that grows completely outside ארץ ישראל, even if its roots may reach inside.

phrases.english: all agree it is exempt!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל גָּדֵל בִּפְטוּר – דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference that step 6 set up and turns it against עולא.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's view that a tree is judged by the soil it draws food from
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies that a tree outside the border is exempt according to everyone, even if its roots draw from ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: The ברייתא describes a tree whose roots are split by a rock
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a case where a rock separates the roots.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? A case where a rock divides the roots.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends עולא by saying the ברייתא is about a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a rock splits the roots, the side outside ארץ ישראל really does not draw from ארץ ישראל soil. So the ברייתא's case does not involve roots feeding across the border. Nothing in it contradicts עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where a rock divides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to עולא in step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is about an ordinary tree whose roots mix across the border.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a tree whose roots are separated by a rock, so it does not contradict עולא.

steps.title: If the roots are separated, why does רבי call the fruit mixed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if a rock separates the roots, what is רבי's reason for saying each fruit is a mix?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is רבי's reasoning?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer. With a rock in the middle, רבי's view of mixed fruit seems hard to understand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the roots are clearly separated, it seems easy to tell which part grew from ארץ ישראל. So why would רבי say each fruit is part טבל and part חולין? The rock answer seems to leave רבי's view without a reason.

phrases.english: If so, what is the reasoning of רבי?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rock answer from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rock answer, as it affects רבי's opinion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Separated roots should allow a clear split, so רבי's 'mixed fruit' seems unjustified.

steps.title: The roots mix again higher up in the tree
steps.stepSummary: The answer: even though the roots are separated, the sap mixes again in the body of the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they become mixed again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי's view: the separation in the roots does not last, because everything mixes again above.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Below the ground the rock keeps the two sides apart. But above it, in the trunk, the food from both sides comes together. So for רבי every fruit still contains a mix.

keyTerms.meaning: They go back, they do it again

phrases.english: Because they then become mixed again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rock keeps the two sides separate all the way up, so רבי has no reason to call the fruit mixed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Above the rock the two sides mix again, so רבי sees every fruit as mixed.

steps.title: So what exactly are they arguing about now?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the basis of the dispute is, now that the case involves a rock.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a new explanation of the argument. With a rock in the case, the old בררה explanation no longer fits well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 explained the argument as being about בררה. Now that the roots are physically separated, the גמרא needs to state anew what רבי and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל really disagree about.

phrases.english: And with regard to what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining רבי's view, the גמרא asks for the root of the dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle the two opinions disagree about, given the rock case.

steps.title: Does the air mix the tree, or does each side stand alone?
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that the air above the ground mixes the tree's food. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that each side stands alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds that the air mixes it. The other holds that this part stands alone and that part stands alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the new basis of the dispute: what happens to the tree above the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the rock separates the roots. רבי says that once the tree rises into the air, everything gets mixed, so every fruit is part טבל and part חולין. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says each side stays separate, as if the tree were cut along the border, so the ארץ ישראל side is obligated and the outside side is exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: With a rock separating the roots, the ברייתא no longer challenges עולא. The argument becomes: רבי says the air mixes the tree, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says each side stands alone.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two 'מר סבר' lines. Here the first one (the air mixes) is רבי. In step 6 the first one (יש ברירה) was רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

phrases.english: One master holds: the air mixes,
phrases.notes: This is רבי. Above the ground, the food from both sides gets mixed together.

phrases.english: and one master holds: this part stands alone
and that part stands alone.
phrases.notes: This is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. He treats the tree as if it were split along the border.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי: the air mixes the parts of the tree. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: each side of the tree stands alone.

steps.title: Do roots really stop at sixteen cubits?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the 16-cubit figure from a משנה that requires a tree to be 25 cubits from a cistern.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do roots only reach sixteen cubits and no more? But we learned in a משנה: a tree must be kept twenty-five cubits away from a cistern!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the idea that tree roots only matter within 16 cubits. It points to a משנה that requires a much bigger distance from a cistern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, roots were treated as affecting the ground only up to 16 cubits. But the משנה requires 25 cubits between a tree and a cistern, which suggests roots reach farther. So the 16-cubit number seems too small.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה?
A cistern, a pit for storing water

phrases.english: And sixteen cubits, and no more?
phrases.notes: This is the 16-cubit distance from earlier in the סוגיא, where roots near the boundary reach into the neighbor's land.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
One must distance a tree from a cistern
twenty-five cubits!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the dispute about the rock and the sap, the גמרא turns to challenge the 16-cubit distance itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that roots affect the ground only within 16 cubits.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה requires 25 cubits from a cistern, which shows roots reach farther than 16 cubits.

steps.title: Roots travel far but only weaken the ground up to sixteen cubits
steps.stepSummary: אביי separates how far roots spread from how far they weaken the soil.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Roots do go far. But they only weaken the ground up to sixteen cubits. Beyond that, they don't weaken it.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by splitting it into two things: how far roots go, and how far they cause damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Roots really can reach past 16 cubits, and that is why a cistern needs 25 cubits of distance. But the 16-cubit rule is about weakening the soil, and roots only do that up to 16 cubits. So the two numbers measure different things and do not contradict each other.

phrases.english: אביי said:
As for spreading, they spread far,
but as for weakening, they do not weaken
except up to sixteen cubits;
beyond that, they do not weaken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since roots reach 25 cubits, the 16-cubit limit seems wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: Roots spread past 16 cubits, which can harm a cistern, but they only weaken the soil within 16 cubits.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two different distances: roots can travel far, but they only weaken the soil within 16 cubits.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks about a tree within sixteen cubits of the boundary
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן what the law is for a tree within 16 cubits of the boundary.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן: What is the law for a tree that is within sixteen cubits of the boundary?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a report from רב דימי. It sets up a question that ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן about a tree close to the boundary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know roots weaken the soil up to 16 cubits, a tree that close to the boundary draws food from the neighbor's ground. The question is what that means for the tree's owner. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: When רב דימי came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן:
A tree that is close to the boundary,
within sixteen cubits, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר, בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the 16-cubit rule that was just confirmed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the status of a tree planted within 16 cubits of the boundary?

steps.title: The owner is a robber and cannot bring בכורים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the owner is a גזלן and may not bring בכורים from the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He is a robber, and one does not bring בכורים from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש's question: the tree's owner is treated like a robber.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the roots weaken the neighbor's ground within 16 cubits, the tree feeds partly off land that is not the owner's. So its fruit is partly taken from someone else, and it cannot be brought as בכורים, which must come from one's own land.

keyTerms.meaning: First fruits brought to the בית המקדש

phrases.english: He said to him: He is a robber,
and one does not bring first fruits from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The owner is a גזלן, and no בכורים may be brought from the tree.

steps.title: A different report: he may bring and recite
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports that רבי יוחנן said the opposite: a tree near the boundary or leaning over it may be used for בכורים with the recitation, because יהושע divided the land on that condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: Whether it is a tree close to the boundary or a tree that leans over, the owner brings בכורים and recites, because יהושע gave the land to ישראל on that condition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of what רבי יוחנן said, and it disagrees with רב דימי's report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבין, the owner of a tree near the boundary, or one that leans into the neighbor's field, may bring בכורים and even say the recitation. The reason is that when יהושע divided ארץ ישראל, it was on the condition that people would not object to these small things. So the fruit counts as fully the owner's.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree that leans over into another's field
He brings (בכורים) and recites the passage
Gave as an inheritance, divided out

steps.confusionAlert: Both reports quote the same רבי יוחנן, but they say opposite things. This is a disagreement about what he actually said, not two different cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of 'the condition יהושע made' explains why some small intrusions on a neighbor's land are allowed in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: When רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן said:
Both a tree that is close to the boundary
and a tree that leans over,
he brings and recites,
phrases.notes: He brings the בכורים and also says the passage that goes with them.

phrases.english: because on this condition יהושע gave
the land to ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a report of רבי יוחנן's view that contradicts רב דימי's report in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tree near the boundary or leaning over it may be used for בכורים with the recitation, because of the condition יהושע set when dividing the land.
steps.whatToRemember: רב דימי: the owner is a גזלן and cannot bring בכורים. רבין: he brings and recites, because of יהושע's condition.

steps.title: New משנה: cutting a tree that leans into a neighbor's field
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a neighbor may cut a leaning tree's branches up to the height of an ox goad held over a plow.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a tree leans into another person's field, the field owner may cut its branches up to the height of an ox goad held over the plow.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with branches that hang over into a neighbor's field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The neighbor does not have to cut the whole overhang. He only clears enough room for plowing, as high as the stick used to drive oxen when it is held up over the plow. Higher branches may stay.

keyTerms.meaning: An ox goad, the stick used to drive oxen

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אִילָן שֶׁהוּא נוֹטֶה לִשְׂדֵה חֲבֵירוֹ –
phrases.english: MISHNA: A tree that leans into the field of another,
he may cut the full height of an ox goad,
phrases.notes: The owner of the field is the one who cuts, so the branches won't block his plowing.

phrases.english: held over the plow.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אִילָן שֶׁהוּא נוֹטֶה לִשְׂדֵה חֲבֵירוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It connects to the leaning tree just mentioned by רבין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A neighbor may cut overhanging branches only up to the height of an ox goad held above a plow.

steps.title: Carob, sycamore and irrigated fields: cut everything over the line
steps.stepSummary: For carob and sycamore trees, and for any tree over an irrigated field, all overhanging branches are cut straight up along the boundary line.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a carob or a sycamore, the branches are cut along the plumb line. Over an irrigated field, any tree's branches are cut along the plumb line.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists cases where the neighbor may cut much more: everything that hangs over his side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Along the plumb line' means cutting every branch that crosses an imaginary line straight up from the boundary. This applies to carob and sycamore trees, which have heavy, shady branches, and to any tree over an irrigated field, where shade does more harm. In these cases the ox-goad limit does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Along the plumb line, straight up from the boundary

phrases.english: And with a carob or a sycamore,
he cuts along the plumb line.
phrases.notes: Picture a weight hanging on a string right over the boundary. Every branch past that line may be cut.

phrases.english: In an irrigated field,
any tree is cut along the plumb line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds cases where more than the ox-goad height may be cut.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carob and sycamore trees, and any tree over an irrigated field, are cut along the plumb line.

steps.title: אבא שאול: all barren trees are cut along the line
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול adds that any tree that does not bear fruit is cut along the plumb line.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: Every barren tree is cut along the plumb line.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with אבא שאול's opinion, which widens the plumb-line rule to all non-fruit trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אבא שאול, it is not only carob and sycamore. Any tree that does not produce fruit gets the strict rule, so the neighbor may cut every branch that crosses the boundary line.

keyTerms.meaning: A barren tree, one that does not bear fruit
A תנא who gives his own view here

steps.whatToRemember: Normal tree: cut only up to the ox-goad height over the plow. Carob, sycamore, or any tree over an irrigated field: cut along the plumb line. אבא שאול: every barren tree is cut along the plumb line.

phrases.english: אבא שאול says:
Every barren tree is cut along the plumb line.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר: כׇּל אִילַן סְרָק כְּנֶגֶד הַמִּשְׁקוֹלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens the plumb-line rule from step 19 to all barren trees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All barren trees are cut along the plumb line.

steps.title: Which clause is אבא שאול talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether אבא שאול's statement about non-fruit trees goes on the רישא of the משנה or on the סיפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא asks: when אבא שאול spoke, was he commenting on the first part of the משנה or on the last part?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question about the end of the משנה. Which earlier rule was אבא שאול reacting to? This question sets up the proofs that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose he is on the רישא, which is about an ordinary field. Then he is adding non-fruit trees to carob and sycamore: in any field, they are cut along the plumb line. Suppose he is on the סיפא, which is about a בית השלחין. Then he is limiting it: only non-fruit trees are cut straight up there, not fruit trees.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among the scholars
The first clause of a משנה or ברייתא
The last clause of a משנה or ברייתא
Is standing on, meaning: is referring to

steps.confusionAlert: Both readings agree that non-fruit trees are cut along the plumb line. The question is about scope. Does אבא שאול add to the rule for ordinary fields? Or does he cut back the rule for a בית השלחין?

phrases.english: GEMARA: A question was asked of them:
Is Abba Shaul referring to the first clause,
phrases.notes: The first clause is the general rule: cut to the height of an ox goad, but cut carob and sycamore straight up.

phrases.english: or is he referring to the last clause?
phrases.notes: The last clause is the rule that every tree over an irrigated field is cut straight up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to attach אבא שאול's statement from step 20 to the earlier clauses of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does אבא שאול's rule about non-fruit trees comment on the רישא (ordinary field) or on the סיפא (בית השלחין)?

steps.title: A ברייתא shows he is talking about the first clause
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes אבא שאול saying that every tree over a בית השלחין is cut along the plumb line. So he does not limit the סיפא, which means he is commenting on the רישא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear a ברייתא: about an irrigated field, אבא שאול says every tree is cut straight up, because shade is bad for it. So he must be talking about the first clause. Yes, learn it from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by bringing a ברייתא with אבא שאול's own words about a בית השלחין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, אבא שאול says every tree over a בית השלחין is cut straight up. So he fully agrees with the סיפא and is not limiting it to non-fruit trees. His statement in the משנה must therefore be an addition to the רישא.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: a source is brought to answer a question
An irrigated field that needs sunlight
Plumb line, meaning cut straight up along the boundary
Learn from this: the point is proven

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught in a baraita:
Regarding an irrigated field, Abba Shaul says:
every tree is cut along the plumb line,
because shade is bad for an irrigated field.
Learn from this: he is referring to the first clause!
Yes, learn it from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 using a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אבא שאול refers to the רישא, since he agrees that all trees over a בית השלחין are cut straight up.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting אבא שאול about a בית השלחין

steps.title: רב אשי: the word 'every' in the משנה proves it too
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי points out that the משנה says כל אילן סרק, every non-fruit tree. The word כל fits an addition to the רישא, not a limit on the סיפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: the wording of the משנה shows this too. It says 'every non-fruit tree.' That fits if he is adding to the first clause. If he were limiting the last clause, he would just have said 'non-fruit trees.' So he must be talking about the first clause. Yes, learn it from here.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a second proof, this time from the exact wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כל (every) widens a rule. It adds all non-fruit trees to carob and sycamore in an ordinary field. In the סיפא, the first תנא already cuts every tree. A limiting opinion would only say אילן סרק, without the word כל.

keyTerms.meaning: Is precise: the wording itself proves the point
A tree that does not bear fruit

steps.whatToRemember: אבא שאול is commenting on the רישא. In an ordinary field, every non-fruit tree is cut along the plumb line, just like carob and sycamore. Over a בית השלחין, all trees are cut straight up.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The mishna's wording also proves this,
since it teaches: "Every non-fruit tree."
Granted, if you say he refers to the first clause,
that is why it says "every tree";
but if you say he refers to the last clause,
he should have just said "a non-fruit tree"!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אַרֵישָׁא קָאֵי?
phrases.english: Rather, isn't it clear that he refers to the first clause?
Yes, learn it from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent proof from the wording of the משנה, backing up step 22's conclusion.
steps.raayaObject: That אבא שאול refers to the רישא
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word כל in the משנה's phrase כל אילן סרק
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אבא שאול adds non-fruit trees to the plumb-line rule for an ordinary field.

steps.title: New משנה: a tree leaning over the public road
steps.stepSummary: A tree leaning into רשות הרבים is cut high enough for a camel with its rider to pass underneath.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a tree leans over the public area, it is cut back so that a camel with its rider can pass under it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It moves from a neighbor's field to the public road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the concern was a neighbor's plowing or field. Now the concern is the public's traffic. The first opinion sets the minimum clearance at the height of a camel with someone riding it.

keyTerms.meaning: The public domain, such as a public road

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ אִילָן שֶׁהוּא נוֹטֶה לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים,
phrases.english: MISHNA: A tree that leans into the public domain,

phrases.aramaic: קוֹצֵץ כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהֵא גָּמָל עוֹבֵר – וְרוֹכְבוֹ.
phrases.english: one cuts it so that a camel can pass, with its rider.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about public space, after the neighbor-field discussion ends in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A tree over רשות הרבים is cut so that a camel with its rider can pass beneath.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: high enough for a loaded camel
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה requires enough clearance for a camel loaded with flax or bundles of branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: cut it high enough for a camel carrying flax or bundles of vine branches.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different measure for how high the branches must be cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He measures by a camel carrying a bulky load, not by a camel with a rider. Which of the two measures is higher is not obvious, and the גמרא takes up that question in step 30.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: גָּמָל טָעוּן פִּשְׁתָּן אוֹ חֲבִילֵי זְמוֹרוֹת.
phrases.english: a camel loaded with flax or bundles of branches.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in step 24 about the required height.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The clearance is measured by a camel loaded with flax or bundles of branches.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: cut everything straight up, because of טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says every overhanging branch must be cut along the plumb line, because of ritual impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the whole tree is cut straight up at the edge of the public area, because of ritual impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a third view. No branches may hang over the public area at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is not concerned only with height clearance for traffic. His reason is טומאה, so he removes the overhang completely. The משנה does not say how טומאה is involved; step 34 explains it.
steps.whyThisMatters: His reason is completely different from the others. They argue about how tall the traffic is, while he is concerned with טומאה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
the whole tree is cut along the plumb line,
because of ritual impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third, stricter opinion than steps 24 and 25, based on a different concern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All branches over רשות הרבים are cut along the plumb line because of טומאה.

steps.title: Which תנא judges damage only by the present?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that for damages we only look at the present situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא who teaches that, with damages, we follow how things look right now?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking whose opinion it follows. The משנה only requires cutting the branches high enough for a camel today, even though they will grow back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The branches will surely grow back into the camel's path. Still, the משנה only demands enough clearance for now. So the משנה assumes we judge damage by the present situation, and the גמרא wants to know which תנא holds that.

keyTerms.meaning: The גמרא section that discusses the משנה
Who is the Tanna (whose opinion is this)?
The present assessment, how things look now

phrases.english: Gemara
Who is the tanna who holds that with damages
we follow the present assessment?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תְּנָא דְּבִנְזָקִין בָּתַר אוּמְדָּנָא דְּהַשְׁתָּא אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the משנה's rules about overhanging trees to ask whose opinion the camel-height rule follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that, for damages, we judge only by the present situation and ignore future growth?

steps.title: ריש לקיש: it is רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who permits digging under רשות הרבים if the cover is strong enough for now.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: This is a disputed matter, and the משנה follows רבי אליעזר. A משנה teaches: You may not dig a hollow under רשות הרבים, such as pits, ditches, or caves. רבי אליעזר permits it if the cover is strong enough for a wagon loaded with stones to drive over it.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers that our משנה is only one side of a מחלוקת. It matches רבי אליעזר, who judges the safety of a covered pit by how strong the cover is now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cover over a pit may rot one day, but רבי אליעזר does not worry about that. He only checks if it holds a loaded wagon today. That is the same idea as cutting branches only for today's camel. The רבנן, who forbid digging at all, would then disagree with our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught as a dispute

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אליעזר does not allow an open pit. The words leave it out, but he means the pit is covered with something strong enough to hold a loaded wagon.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
It is taught as a dispute,
and it is the view of Rabbi Eliezer.
As we learned: One may not make a hollow space
beneath the public domain,
pits, ditches, or caves.
Rabbi Eliezer permits it,
if it is covered enough that a wagon can travel on it
while loaded with stones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: בְּמַחֲלוֹקֶת שְׁנוּיָה, וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 27 by naming רבי אליעזר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי אליעזר, who judges a pit cover by its strength now and ignores future rot.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about digging under רשות הרבים, where רבי אליעזר allows it with a cover strong enough for a loaded wagon.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: it can even fit the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה can match the רבנן too, because a pit cover rots unseen while branches are cut as they grow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: You can even say it follows the רבנן. There, the cover sometimes weakens and the owner does not notice. But here, each time a branch grows, he cuts it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer. He says our משנה does not have to be only רבי אליעזר's view, because the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן forbid the pit because the cover can rot underground and no one will think to check it. A branch is out in the open, so the owner sees it grow and cuts it each time. So even the רבנן can agree that clearing the branches for now is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: On his mind, something he pays attention to

steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש says only רבי אליעזר fits the משנה. רבי יוחנן says even the רבנן fit, because a hidden danger can be forgotten but a visible one gets handled.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
You can even say it is the Rabbis,
there, sometimes the cover weakens
and it is not on his mind,
but here,
each one as it comes, he cuts it off.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to Step 27 and rejects the need to limit the משנה to רבי אליעזר, as ריש לקיש did.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה can fit the רבנן as well, since a hidden pit cover is forgotten but growing branches are seen and cut.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: ריש לקיש's comparison misses that the pit is hidden while the branches are visible.

steps.title: Whose measure is higher, רבי יהודה's or the רבנן's?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's measure from the משנה and asks whether it is higher or lower than the רבנן's measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: a camel loaded with flax or bundles of branches. They asked: Is רבי יהודה's measure bigger, or maybe the רבנן's measure is bigger?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה again to start a new topic. It asks which measure needs more clearance: a camel with its rider, or a camel loaded with flax or branches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said a camel with its rider must pass. רבי יהודה said a camel loaded with flax or branches must pass. It is not obvious which is taller, so the גמרא asks which opinion makes the owner cut more.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked before them

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
a camel loaded with flax
or bundles of branches.
A question was asked before them:
Is Rabbi Yehuda's measure bigger,
or perhaps the Rabbis' measure is bigger?
phrases.notes: The Rabbis' measure is the camel with its rider, from the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: שִׁיעוּרָא דְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְפִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the question of whose opinion the משנה follows and returns to the משנה's dispute about the height of clearance.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which measure requires more clearance: a camel with its rider (רבנן) or a camel loaded with flax or branches (רבי יהודה)?

steps.title: The רבנן's measure must be the higher one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the רבנן's measure is clearly higher. If רבי יהודה's were higher, the רבנן would have no way to deal with a loaded camel.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that the רבנן's measure is greater! Because if you think רבי יהודה's measure is greater, then what would the רבנן do in the case of רבי יהודה's measure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 30 and says the רבנן's measure, a camel with its rider, is the higher one. It proves this by showing the opposite would leave the רבנן with no solution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the רבנן require room for a camel with its rider, and רבי יהודה requires room for a camel loaded with flax or bundles of branches. If the loaded camel were taller, a loaded camel could not get under branches cut to the רבנן's lower height. A load cannot bend, so the רבנן's view would not work in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: If it enters your mind, if you were to think

phrases.english: It is obvious that the Rabbis' measure is greater!
For if it enters your mind
that Rabbi Yehuda's measure is greater,

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּנַן – בְּשִׁיעוּרָא דְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הֵיכִי עָבְדִי?
phrases.english: how would the Rabbis act in the case of Rabbi Yehuda's measure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30 about which measure is higher.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which measure is higher, the רבנן's or רבי יהודה's?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן's measure is higher. Otherwise their view could not handle loaded camels.

steps.title: But then how does רבי יהודה handle a rider?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. If the רבנן's measure is higher, רבי יהודה's lower measure would seem to leave a camel with a rider stuck.
steps.simpleTranslation: But rather, what are you saying, that the רבנן's measure is greater? Then what does רבי יהודה do in the case of the רבנן's measure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. The same problem seems to come back the other way, this time against רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof in step 31 rested on the idea that each opinion must work for every kind of traffic. Camels with riders also travel the road. So if the rider is higher, רבי יהודה's lower cut seems not to work either, and the proof seems to cancel itself out.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather, what? A phrase used to turn the argument back around

phrases.english: But rather, what? The Rabbis' measure is greater?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה – בְּשִׁיעוּרָא דְּרַבָּנַן מַאי עָבֵיד?
phrases.english: Then what does Rabbi Yehuda do in the case of the Rabbis' measure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 31 by applying the same reasoning against רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof in step 31 that the רבנן's measure is higher
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If every opinion must allow all traffic to pass, רבי יהודה's lower measure fails for a camel with a rider, just as the other way would fail for the רבנן.

steps.title: A rider can bend down
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that a rider can duck down and pass under the branches, but a load cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is possible for him to bend down and pass underneath it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A person riding a camel can bend over and get under the branches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases are not equal. A rider can make himself shorter, but a load cannot. So רבי יהודה's lower measure still works for riders, while a lower measure could never work for a loaded camel. This confirms that the רבנן's measure is the higher one.
steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן's measure, a camel with its rider, is higher than רבי יהודה's loaded camel. רבי יהודה still works because a rider can duck, but a load cannot.

phrases.english: It is possible that he bends down
phrases.notes: 'He' is the rider sitting on the camel.

phrases.english: and passes underneath it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32 and keeps the answer of step 31 in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the two cases are different
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both measures face the same problem, so neither can be shown to be higher.
steps.terutzMaskana: A rider can bend down but a load cannot, so the רבנן's measure is the higher one.

steps.title: A ברייתא explains רבי שמעון's reason as a tent of impurity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון's words from the משנה again. A ברייתא explains that 'because of טומאה' means טומאה passed through a tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the whole tree is cut along the plumb line, because of טומאה. It was taught: because of the tent of טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רבי שמעון's line in the משנה, which was introduced in step 26. It now brings a ברייתא that spells out what kind of טומאה he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the worry is אהל הטומאה. A branch over something impure, such as a dead body, acts like a roof. It then spreads the impurity to people walking underneath it on the public road.

keyTerms.meaning: Plumb line, the straight-down line from the edge of the property
It was taught, in a ברייתא
Impurity spread by a covering or 'tent' over something impure

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
the whole tree is cut along the plumb line,
because of ritual impurity.
It was taught: because of the tent of impurity.
phrases.notes: The branch works like a roof over something impure, such as a dead body, and makes people under it impure too.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הָאִילָן כְּנֶגֶד הַמִּשְׁקוֹלֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the two measures and goes back to רבי שמעון's view in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון's 'because of טומאה' refers to אהל הטומאה, impurity spread by the branch acting as a roof.

steps.title: Why did the ברייתא need to say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא's explanation is needed, since the משנה already said 'because of טומאה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious! We learned in the משנה 'because of טומאה'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Its point seems to add nothing new to what the משנה already says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption here is that the only way a branch could cause impurity is by acting as a tent. If so, the משנה's words already say everything the ברייתא says.

phrases.english: That is obvious!
We learned 'because of ritual impurity'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא quoted in step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's explanation 'because of the tent of טומאה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already says 'because of טומאה', so the ברייתא seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Without the ברייתא we might blame only crows
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה alone, we might think the worry is a crow dropping something impure, and a scarecrow would solve that. The ברייתא teaches that the real worry is the tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had the משנה, I would have said: perhaps a crow brings something impure and throws it there, and a mere scarecrow would be enough. So the ברייתא teaches us that the worry is the tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the ברייתא is needed. It shows there was a different way to read the משנה, and the ברייתא rules that reading out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worry were only a crow dropping impure things from the branch, a scarecrow would be enough and there would be no need to cut the branch. By saying the problem is the tent, the ברייתא explains why the whole overhanging branch must be cut.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said, a mistaken first idea

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's reason is אהל הטומאה, the branch acting as a roof over impurity. That is why a scarecrow is not enough and the whole branch must be cut.

phrases.english: If it were only from the Mishnah,
I would have said:
perhaps a crow brings something impure
and throws it there,
phrases.notes: The crow sits on the branch and drops the impure thing onto the public road.

phrases.english: and a mere scarecrow would be enough;
so it teaches us:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 35 by showing the ברייתא adds something new.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ruling out a mistaken first reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's טומאה is about crows dropping impure items, so a scarecrow would be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: The worry is אהל הטומאה, so the branch itself must be cut.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter לא יחפור
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the chapter לא יחפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter לא יחפור.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the chapter לא יחפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional goodbye to a finished chapter, with the hope of coming back to learn it again. It is not part of the argument itself.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, said when finishing a chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter Lo Yachpor

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of the chapter לא יחפור.
